source.ref: https://github.com/ollama/ollama/pull/9379; hand-checked 2026-09-28; the pull request's next commit, 927a601cb, fixed nested-path, files-omitted-error and nested-test-case

rationale: Path handling in model creation: a real failure on nested paths (not in AACR-Bench's references) and the Windows separator gap the references do name. ADR-0036: file-path-error is optional, since the 400 list it names is outside the change (the change does introduce errFilePath and the nested-path failure that reaches it). files-omitted-error is required: true at head, in the change, fixed by the author's next commit, and now in ocra's own words. nested-test-case stays optional: a test exercising inputs production never sends is a minor defect, found in one run, and waits for the second rater. windows-separator is optional and marked for vetting again: os.Root still contains such paths, so on Windows the only effect is file-path-error's 500 instead of a 400, the same defense-in-depth class as three adapter-path findings labelled invalid, the merged pull request kept the gap, and only a model's reference vouches for it, at suggestion; its range is narrowed to the separator checks. Fingerprint 165fe552 keeps both labels: they are two claims on the same code (ADR-0012), and a label applies to its own title first.

expect.concern: root.OpenFile creates the file before any parent directory exists (MkdirAll runs later, in createLink), so a nested path such as dir/model.safetensors fails with ENOENT and is reported as an invalid path.
validRelative checks only '/' as a separator, so on Windows a drive-letter or backslash path passes the early check; os.Root still contains it, so the request ends in a 500 instead of a 400.
The 400 list for base-model file errors omits errFilePath, which the adapters' list includes, so a bad path in files gets a 500 instead of a 400.
files is always replaced with a non-nil map, so a request without files skips the neither-from-nor-files check and gets an unknown-type error instead.
The test passes nested/../ and ./ paths straight to convertFromSafetensors, which the handler's validRelative rejects, so it covers inputs production never sends.
